hook: 2-person spring cleanup: the guess says $193. The math says $595
hook_say: Here is why a spring cleanup priced from a $24 hourly guess comes in about $400 low.

rows.label: Hours on site, spring cleanup
rows.why: A spring cleanup in the calculator's presets takes 4 hours on site.

rows.label: People on the job
rows.why: Two people work it, so every hour on site and on the road counts twice.

rows.label: Round-trip miles, supplies
rows.why: A 10-mile round trip at 30 mph adds 20 minutes per person, plus 76 cents a mile and $20 of bags and supplies.

rows.label: The guess: $24.07 an hour x 8 person-hours
rows.why: Divide $52,000 of take-home pay by every hour worked in a year and you get $24.07. Times 2 people for 4 hours, that prices the job at $193, with no drive time, supplies, costs or tax.

rows.label: Break-even rate per paid hour
rows.why: Add self-employment tax, an estimated 12% income tax and $545 a month of business costs, then spread it over paid hours only, since only 65% of hours worked get billed: break-even is $54.80 an hour.

rows.label: Price floor, zero profit
rows.why: 8 person-hours on site plus 40 minutes of crew driving at $54.80, plus $7.60 of mileage and $20 of supplies: $502 just to break even.

fix.label: Quote with 15% profit
fix.why: Build in a 15% profit margin and round up to the next $5: $595 for the cleanup. The Price Sheet does this for every job type at once.

note: Example numbers from the calculator's presets. Yours go in the yellow cells.
